scope: An independent model family added to the ladder, and the boundary test its disclosed cutoff makes possible.

verdict.family_check: At the shared 2025-era boundary the new family behaves like the Qwen rung of comparable size: llama3_8b 1.206 vs qwen7b -2.983, both with intervals spanning zero. The paper's claim that no cliff is established below ~100B at that boundary is not a Qwen artifact.
verdict.boundary_check: At Llama-3-8B's OWN disclosed boundary the picture is different: it drops 13.608 F1 (CI [0.732, 26.534]) where the same-scale control drops 1.315. The difference-in-differences is 12.293 (CI [-5.044, 30.11], p=0.16677).
verdict.what_it_means: An 8B model shows a significant boundary gap when the boundary is the one its vendor documents, on questions where a same-scale Qwen rung shows nothing. Taken at face value that says the paper's 'no cliff below ~100B' finding is specific to a SHARED 2025 boundary sitting inside most rungs' training windows.
verdict.how_far_this_goes: Not as far as the point estimates suggest. The raw Llama-3-8B drop is significant, but the difference-in-differences that separates the cutoff from year-to-year difficulty drift is 11.209 with CI [-3.423, 25.313] (p=0.12517) even in the better-powered pooled-post specification, which does NOT exclude zero. The result is control-dependent: of the three same-questions controls, only 1 of 3 gives an interval excluding zero, and we quote the pre-specified same-scale control rather than the one that does. Four noisy quantities are differenced across ~30 quizzes on the pre side. We therefore report this as a consistent, sizeable, directionally clear signal that this design cannot certify.
verdict.caveat: One model with a disclosed cutoff is one data point, and it cannot separate 'Llama-3 has an earlier cutoff' from 'Llama-3 was trained differently'. Establishing the boundary-position account needs several families with disclosed cutoffs at matched scales, which is a data-availability problem: seven of our nine vendors publish no cutoff at all.
